title: Selling ice cream in the Red Light District and its closing
summary: Bands heard in the District 1929-37 and its replacement by a housing project.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What about when you were going out on the selling ice cream, where did you sell ice cream? I was in the old Red Light District there.

Mm-hmm. And I heard a lot of good bands out there too. Joe Robichio, to hear... I saw the trumpet man, that's the downtown, yeah, on the Coliseum. Oh yeah, he hit Renee. Mm-hmm. He played a fine trumpet. He drank a lot of wine. He killed him.
About what year would it be you would be going around the District? Oh, well, 1929, 30, all the way up to 37, I believe. Mm-hmm.
And after that, they shut it down or something. And they made a housing project out of it. Yeah. So about 37 was closed down. See, about that time. I don't know. Mm-hmm.
And when did they build that housing project in there? I can't remember whether that was before the war or during the war. Mm-hmm.
It was before the war. Before the war. I'm not quite sure it was. Mm-hmm.
I wasn't down there, but I heard people go to the war. I mean, it was real.
I think they should have another one like that down in the office. It was a big help, you know.
It helped business and all, you know. brought a lot of people in the town, I guess, the sailors. And the sailors and all the businessmen coming from. That's right.
